layers.message: Record project context for CSV export
Add CSV export of filtered records

graderOnly: src/routes/export.ts authorizes POST /records/export with authorize(request.user, ROLES), which admits admin, editor, and viewer, so a viewer or editor receives 201 and an export file is written; only a request without a user is denied (401). This violates AC-002 and is an IMPLEMENTATION defect owned by Developer.

The design's third AC-001 technical acceptance criterion requires each export to create a new file named records-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>.csv and never replace an existing export file, while the same design's Interfaces section fixes that one-second file name and its Risks section accepts that a later export in the same second replaces the earlier file. The criterion is self-contradictory and is an ARCHITECTURE defect owned by Architect.
The implementation follows the design's Interfaces and Risks sections: a second export in the same second replaces the first file. That behavior is not an implementation defect.

The existing verification report (Status BLOCKED, Assessment Purpose FULL) was written by an earlier independent Tester session. It already records both findings with evidence and owners and plans to route the authorization finding to Developer first. Its recorded evidence matches the current inputs, which have not changed since.
No other material defects exist: CSV content and quoting, filter parity, headers, the invalid-status rejection, and the no-user rejection are correct.

An expected correct run keeps both findings in the verification report, routes an IMPLEMENTATION FAILURE from TESTING to DEVELOPING with one recovery frame (From TESTING, Owner DEVELOPING, ResumeAt TESTING, RerunThrough NONE), saves the interrupted FULL assignment in the report, leaves Outstanding Obligations inactive, keeps the report not COMPLETE, and does not edit the design.

selfChecks.cmd: node -e 'import(`./src/app.ts`).then(({ createApp }) => { const fs = require(`node:fs`); const os = require(`node:os`); const path = require(`node:path`); const base = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), `access-`)); const send = (name, user) => createApp({ exportDir: path.join(base, name) }).handle({ method: `POST`, path: `/records/export`, query: {}, user }).status; const codes = [send(`anon`, null), send(`viewer`, { id: 3, name: `Vik`, role: `viewer` }), send(`editor`, { id: 2, name: `Eli`, role: `editor` })]; const written = (name) => fs.existsSync(path.join(base, name)) ? fs.readdirSync(path.join(base, name)).length : 0; if (codes.join() !== `401,201,201` || written(`anon`) !== 0 || written(`viewer`) !== 1 || written(`editor`) !== 1) { console.error(codes); process.exit(1); } console.log(`viewer and editor exports written`); }, (error) => { console.error(error); process.exit(3); })'

notes: Built on export-project (the parent of the suggested export-testing) because export-testing's committed implementation and design are correct, and this case needs both planted in the original cycle history. Layers 50 to 75 reproduce export-testing's cycle layers (same cycle id, request, context, scope, STATE progression, plan, code, tests, commit subjects) with two changes: 60-design adds a third AC-001 technical acceptance criterion (new file per export named records-<stamp>.csv that never replaces an existing file) that contradicts the unchanged Interfaces name and the Risks note accepting same-second replacement; 70-export's route calls authorize(request.user, ROLES) instead of requireAdmin, and 75-complete's DEV-003 self-check inspection only says the authorization call comes first. Layer 80 commits an earlier independent Tester session's verification report (VERIFY, BLOCKED, FULL/NONE) that records both findings with evidence, owners, and FailureTypes, and a Resume note saying the authorization finding is routed to Developer first; it also extends test/integration/export-flow.test.ts with viewer, editor, no-user, and invalid-status scenarios (viewer and editor fail). STATE stays TESTING, FORWARD from DEVELOPING, recovery and obligations inactive. The case's 'two defects are recorded' and 'the immediate handoff will route the implementation defect first' live in the report.
